how_to_run: python3 run_eval.py <eval-id> <out-dir> builds the fixture, runs the skill from the plugin under test, and (for interview evals) a simulated student from students/ (decided R10-5). Grade with python3 grade_eval.py <out-dir>. Expected text is copied from deconstruct-redesign.md section 2 and verification-decisions.md; never retype it.

evals.name: sales-pre-call-brief
evals.expected_output: Backlog choice, then the five-part interview in order with the recipe in Part 3, a method follow-up for the step after the student stops, today-versus-ideal follow-up, fixed and gate questions, the four Part 5 draft messages, Value & Measurement close, the labels preview, and a saved single requirements file.
expectations: The first message contains the opening said exactly as in the spec (section 2), beginning "Deconstruct turns this workflow into a clear, testable description of what it must do.", followed by the switch line "I'll explain the questions that need it, and 'not sure' is always a fine answer. If you've done this before, say 'skip the explanations'."

Each part opens with "Part N of 5" and its name (Part 1 What this is worth … Part 5 Rules, where you check or approve its work, the sources it uses, and how you'll judge it), and no part announces its own time
Every AI message asks at most one question (a draft message ending "What's wrong or missing?" counts as one)
The label "Ask:" never appears in any AI message
The words step-driven and goal-driven never appear in any AI message, and the AI never asks the student to choose a path type

`requirements.md` has these sections in this order: `# [Name] — Workflow Requirements`, `## Goal`, `## Value & Measurement`, `## Metadata`, `## Path`, `## Inputs`, `## Context Inventory`, `## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Example Scenarios`, `## Rules & Constraints`, `## Human Gates`, `## Security, Privacy & Safety`; no YAML frontmatter; no `Definition Type` row; no `## Sequence` and no `## Optimization Notes`
`## Human Gates` opens with the line `Runs: with you` or `Runs: without you`
`## Security, Privacy & Safety` contains the line `Governing regime: …` before a `### Writes` heading; under `### Writes` there is either a `- W1 · …` line or the line `None`
Every line under `## Path` that is a step is written `- Step N — [Name] · produces …` with a `fixed (…)` or `flexible` mark, tags in the spec's order
`framework/[name]/deconstruct-in-progress.md` existed during the interview (after Part 2) and is deleted once `requirements.md` is written
The close says "Workflow Requirements saved to `framework/[name]/requirements.md`." with the counts, names Step 3 Design and "run the design skill", and mentions `/design`
The Workflow node has `status: under-development`, links `[Requirements](framework/[name]/requirements.md)` in `# Artifacts`, and has no `definition_type` written by this run
Phase 1 asks "Which workflow from your backlog do you want to map?" with today's Why and Not sure? lines, and the Why does not mention step-driven
Part 2's last question is "Is there a law or regulation that governs this work?"; after "no", no detail table and no regulation questions appear
Part 3 shows the recipe by name: "We'll shape this in three steps: say it, sharpen it, make it checkable."
The goal sentence played back has no "containing" blank, and a second playback after the send-back test begins "Here's your goal now:"
`## Acceptance Criteria` uses the form `1. **AC1 (must)** — …` with one or two (must) checks and a `Reference example:` line naming the real output's C# ID
"never name another client" is recorded as a Must never rule in `## Rules & Constraints`, not as an acceptance criterion

The AI asks "What comes after that?" after the student's method stops, then "Is that how you do it today, or is it different?", then asks "Today you also … Should that stay?" about the LinkedIn-notes workaround
The CRM-check step is recorded as `fixed (policy)`
Decision line D1 is recorded with `settled by: a rule on a value`

Part 5 is delivered as four draft messages: messages 1–3 end "What's wrong or missing?"; message 2 introduces context with "These are the sources it uses, what we call its **context**"; message 4 ends with the Hand-it-back text
The test inputs are saved as `framework/[name]/inputs/E<n>-<short-name>.md`, numbered from E1, with E1 the input behind the Golden Example

evals.name: built-not-tested-continue

sessions.prompt: Run the deconstruct skill. Continue my workflow.

evals.expected_output: No re-run: the resume orientation sends the workflow to its next skill (Test).
expectations: The AI does not say the Deconstruct opening and asks no interview question
The AI orients the student: Step 4 (Build) is done and Step 5 (Test) is next, and routes to Test
`requirements.md` and `design-spec.md` are unchanged; no file is renamed

evals.name: running-with-requirements

sessions.prompt: Run the deconstruct skill for Weekly Status Report. I want to change its requirements.

expectations: The AI says "This workflow already has a Design Plan, so changes to its requirements go through Improve. Say 'run the improve skill'."
The AI does not say the Deconstruct opening and asks no interview question
The node's `status` stays `in-production`; no file changes

evals.name: running-work-from-analyze

sessions.prompt: Run the deconstruct skill for Stakeholder Meeting Prep.
Run the deconstruct skill. Continue my workflow.

evals.expected_output: The running-work message in both sessions; status kept.
expectations: Session 1: the AI says "This workflow is already running, so it isn't set up for Deconstruct yet. Keep running it as it is for now."
Session 2 ("continue my workflow"): the AI says the same running-work message and does not start Step 2
Neither session says the Deconstruct opening or asks an interview question
The node's `status` stays `in-production`; no file is written

evals.name: rerun-resume-then-set-aside

sessions.prompt: Run the deconstruct skill. Continue my workflow.

evals.expected_output: Resumes the re-run at Part 4 with the resume line; the Design Spec is set aside only when the new requirements are saved.
expectations: The first AI message uses the resume line ("Last time we covered [Parts 1 to N]; I noted [short summary].") naming Parts 1 to 3, then the Part 4 signpost; it does not say the opening
`design-spec.md` is still present and linked until the new `requirements.md` is saved

When the new `requirements.md` is saved, `design-spec.md` is renamed `design-spec-YYYY-MM-DD.md`, its `# Artifacts` link is removed, and the AI says "Your Design Plan was built on the old requirements, so I've set it aside. Design will make a new one."
The old `requirements.md` is saved with a date suffix; the new one has the new sections (no `Definition Type` row)
`deconstruct-in-progress.md` is deleted at the end

evals.name: renamed-resume-from-other-skills
evals.expected_output: Build and Design each say Deconstruct is unfinished for Monthly Risk Register and route there; Deconstruct resumes with the resume line.
expectations: Session 1 (Build): the AI says Deconstruct is unfinished for Monthly Risk Register (or Program Risk Register) and routes to Deconstruct; it builds nothing
Session 2 (Design): the same, and it writes no Design Plan

Session 3 (Deconstruct): the first AI message uses the resume line ("Last time we covered [Parts 1 to N]; I noted [short summary].") naming Parts 1 to 3, then the Part 4 signpost; it does not say the opening and does not show the backlog choice
Session 3 merges into `registry/workflows/program-risk-register.md` (the progress file's `Workflow node:`), not a new node

evals.name: cold-entry-unfinished
evals.expected_output: Test lists Vendor Invoice Intake as an unfinished workflow and routes to Deconstruct; Deconstruct resumes it.
expectations: Session 1 (Test): the AI names Vendor Invoice Intake as a workflow partway through Deconstruct and routes there; it opens no test round
Session 2 (Deconstruct): the resume line naming Parts 1 to 2, then the Part 3 signpost; no opening

evals.name: other-workflow-unfinished

sessions.prompt: Run the deconstruct skill for Onboarding Checklist Drafting.

evals.expected_output: One line naming the unfinished Monthly Risk Register, then a fresh interview for Onboarding Checklist Drafting.
expectations: The AI mentions the unfinished workflow in one line, in the form "[Name] is partway through Deconstruct; say 'continue my workflow' for that one." with [Name] the Monthly Risk Register
The AI then starts Onboarding Checklist Drafting with the opening ("Deconstruct turns this workflow into a clear, testable description of what it must do."); it does not resume the other workflow

The node's `status` stays `retired`; no file changes

Run the deconstruct skill for Weekly Status Report.
Run the deconstruct skill for Weekly Status Report.

Session 1 never tells the student to say 'continue my workflow'
Session 2: after "no", the re-run starts (the opening, then prefill from the old file)
Session 3 (`readiness: not-ready`, round complete): "This workflow is built but isn't running yet, so the next step is to finish it. Say 'run the build skill'."; the R9-3 question is not asked
Session 4 (`readiness: ready`): "This workflow is built but isn't running yet, so the next step is to finish it. Say 'run the run skill'."; the R9-3 question is not asked
Session 5 (round in progress): "This workflow is built but isn't running yet, so the next step is to finish it. Say 'run the test skill'."; the R9-3 question is not asked

evals.name: old-format-rerun

sessions.prompt: Run the deconstruct skill for Weekly Status Report. I want to redo its requirements.

evals.expected_output: Re-run with prefill from the old step-driven file; step and E numbers kept; old file saved with a date suffix.
expectations: The AI says the opening (a fresh interview), then prefills every part from the old file (value, name and regulation included) for the student to confirm
The four old steps keep their numbers (Step 1 Pull updates … Step 4 Save & log); E1 to E3 keep their numbers and a new input is E4
The old file is saved as `requirements-YYYY-MM-DD.md`; the new `requirements.md` has no `Definition Type` row, no `## Sequence`, no `## Optimization Notes`
The Slack summary is a `W1 · …` line under `### Writes` naming Step 4
`definition_type` is left on the node as it was
